sentences.text: Learned Aga has filed a counter affidavit today in Court, which is taken on record.
2. Heard learned counsel for the petitioners, learned A.G.A. for the State, Shri Om Prakash, learned counsel for respondent no.3 and perused the record.
3. The instant writ petition seeks quashing of the FIR dated 16.08.2024 giving rise to Case Crime No. 60 of 2024, under Sections 376, 452, 504, 506 IPC, Police Station- Shahganj, District- Sonbhadra.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioners has submitted that from the allegation made in the first information report, prima facie no offence, complained of, is disclosed against the petitioners.

5. Per contra, learned AGA as well as learned counsel for respondent no.3 have submitted that during the course of investigation the statement of the victim has been recorded under Section 183 of BNSS, in which, specific role of committing the offence of rape upon the victim has been alleged against petitioner no.1 Ramchandar.
Learned AGA has further submitted that as against petitioner no.2-Anish, no offence under Section 376 IPC has been found and as such, he has been charge-sheeted only under Section 504 and 506 IPC.

Learned AGA has further submitted that from the allegation made in the first information report, prima facie offence is clearly disclosed against the petitioners and, as such, the first information report cannot be quashed in view of the law laid down by the Supreme Court in the case of State of Telangana Vs. Habib Abdullah Jellani reported in (2017) 2 SCC 779, Neeharika Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd. vs. State of Maharashtra and Others reported in (2021) SCC Online SC 315 and in a recent decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Criminal Appeal No. 843 of 2024, Directorate Enforcement Vs. Niraj Tyagi and others.

sentences.text: 6. Having considered the rival submissions made by learned counsel for the parties and taking into consideration the submissions made by learned AGA and learned counsel for respondent no.3 and in view of the statement made by the victim clearly stating therein that petitioner no.1 Ramchandar has committed offence of rape upon her and that the other co-accused Anish has already been charge-sheeted under Section 504 and 506 IPC as such, keeping in view the relevant law cited by learned A.G.A. for the State and the fact that impugned F.I.R. prima facie discloses cognizable offence against the petitioners and noting the submissions made by learned AGA, we are of the opinion that impugned first information report can not be quashed.

8. However, in case, the petitioners file an application for anticipatory/ regular bail before the appropriate Court, their bail application be considered and disposed of as expeditiously as possible,
in accordance with law.
9. With these observations, the instant writ petition is disposed of.
